key_insight: The paper shows that neuromorphic AI can be made both faster and more energy efficient by designing the spiking network and the hardware together. A dual memory pathway architecture achieves over 4× higher throughput and 5× better energy efficiency while using 40–60% fewer parameters.
problem_solved: Neuromorphic systems often struggle to balance performance, efficiency, and model size when deployed on hardware. This work addresses the gap between algorithm design and chip constraints by co-optimizing both for efficient real-world execution.
method: Designs a spiking neural network with two memory pathways to improve computation and state handling.
Co-designs the network architecture with a custom neuromorphic chip so the model matches hardware capabilities.
Reduces parameter count while improving throughput and energy efficiency compared with state-of-the-art implementations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates a practical path to deploy spiking models that are smaller, faster, and far more energy efficient. It is especially relevant for edge AI and always-on applications where power and latency are critical.

paper_title: Algorithm–hardware co-design of neuromorphic networks with dual memory pathways
paper_authors: Pengfei Sun, Zhe Su, Jascha Achterberg, Giacomo Indiveri, Dan F. M. Goodman
